1_1.title: Management Cybersecurity Training
1_1.description: Management takes part in cybersecurity training on a regular basis (§38(3) BSIG). The law sets no fixed interval; recommendation: every 3 years and whenever the management body changes.

1_4.title: Personal Liability Acknowledgment
1_4.description: Management confirms awareness of the liability rule in §38(2) BSIG (internal liability under company law). Not a statutory confirmation duty, but robust governance evidence for §38(1).

2_4.title: Risk Acceptance & IS Policy Approval
2_4.description: Management approves the information security policy and accepts the residual risks from the risk register (2.3). Art. 20(1) NIS2 has management bodies approve the measures and oversee them; §38(1) BSIG has them implement and oversee them. For the entity types the CIR covers, management bodies review the policy at least annually and after significant incidents or significant changes to operations or risks (CIR 1.1.2), the risk assessment and treatment plan are reviewed on the same occasions (CIR 2.1.4), and residual risks may also be accepted by accountable persons who report to management (CIR 2.1.1).

3_2.title: Detection, Classification & Logging
3_2.description: Set up a classification scheme (significant incident, §2 Nr. 11 BSIG), a reporting channel for suspicious events, detection processes and a complete incident log. Recurring incidents must be assessed on a quarterly basis (CIR 3.4.2(b)): incidents sharing the same apparent root cause that occur at least twice within six months and collectively meet the financial loss criterion count together as one significant incident (CIR Article 4).

3_3.title: BSI Reporting Readiness (24h/72h/1M)
3_3.description: Build the BSI reporting process: 24h early warning, 72h notification, intermediate report on BSI request, final report one month after the 72h notification (§32(1) BSIG). Set up reporting portal access and responsibilities. Reporting readiness is tested at planned intervals (CIR 3.5.5); no fixed interval is prescribed, recommendation: annually.

6_2.title: Secure Development & Configuration
6_2.description: Establish secure development guidelines (SDLC) and configuration baselines.

6_3.title: Vulnerability Management
6_3.description: Implement vulnerability management with scanning, risk-based prioritisation and a disclosure process; document deliberate non-remediation.

7_1.title: Security KPIs & Metrics
7_1.description: Define measurable security KPIs and report them at a self-set rhythm with trends and thresholds (recommendation: quarterly).

7_3.title: Management Review
7_3.description: Management oversees the implementation of the measures (§38(1) BSIG), and their effectiveness is assessed by a set procedure (§30(2) Nr. 6 BSIG). For the entity types the CIR covers, the company also regularly reviews compliance with its policies, and management receives regular reports on the state of information security (CIR 2.2.1). No fixed interval is prescribed; recommendation: an annual management review with a gap analysis.

8_3.title: Role-Specific & Management Training
8_3.description: Specialised training for roles with security duties, including on role changes. Management training is evidenced under 1.1.

8_4.title: Training Effectiveness & Phishing Simulations
8_4.description: Measure the effectiveness of training and awareness (§30(2) Nr. 6 BSIG). Phishing simulations are an established method, not a legal duty; involve the works council and data protection first.

9_3.title: Key & Certificate Management
9_3.description: Document and implement key and certificate management across the full lifecycle (e.g. key vault or HSM where appropriate).

10_4.title: Access Reviews
10_4.description: Review and document access rights including privileged accounts on a regular basis. Legally: at planned intervals; recommendation: yearly, privileged accounts quarterly.

11_1.title: Authentication: where MFA is mandatory
11_1.description: Roll out MFA risk-based and document exceptions with compensating controls. Recommended order: admin accounts first, then internet-facing services, then the remaining systems.

11_3.title: Authentication Standards
11_3.description: Review authentication procedures and the password policy against current standards on a regular basis (NIST SP 800-63B, BSI IT-Grundschutz ORP.4).

12_2.title: BSI Registration
12_2.description: Set up the MUK account, complete the registration in the BSI portal and submit all mandatory data. Statutory deadline: at the latest three months after the company first qualifies as an essential or important entity (§33(1) BSIG). For entities in scope since the BSIG entered into force on 6 December 2025, that window ended on 6 March 2026; registration is then due immediately.

12_3.title: Registration Maintenance
12_3.description: Report changes to registration data to the BSI without delay, at the latest within two weeks (§33(5) BSIG); additionally verify the data annually and keep the contact person reachable.

12_4.title: Compliance Evidence
12_4.description: Maintain documentation of implementation on an ongoing basis (§30(1) S. 3 BSIG). Only for operators of critical facilities: evidence every 3 years (§39) and attack detection (§31(2)); special registration under §34 only for the entity types of §60(1) BSIG.
